newsitem.title: JAPAN: Iridium to launch first satellites in December.
newsitem.headline: Iridium to launch first satellites in December.

text.p: The international communications consortium Iridium will make its first satellite launch this December, when three of its satellites will be fired into orbit, a Japanese partner in the venture said on Thursday.
A spokesman for Japanese telecommunications firm DDI Corp said the announcement of the launch plans was made on Wednesday by Iridium LLC chairman Robert Kinzie in the western Japanese city of Kyoto.

Iridium is an international consortium funding the development of the Iridium system, which is expected to be the first network for worldwide wireless telecommunications services via hand-held telephones and pagers.
The project, led by Motorola Inc of the United States, aims eventually to provide global cellular telephone services using 66 communications satellites. The services are scheduled to start in 1998.
DDI is taking part in the project through Iridium's Japanese arm, Nippon Iridium Corp.
The satellites will be launched in California.
